newsitem.title: USA: Clinton FY '98 budget seeks $7.3 bln for Interior.
newsitem.headline: Clinton FY '98 budget seeks $7.3 bln for Interior.

text.p: The Interior Department budget would increase three percent to $7.299 billion, up from FY 1997's $7.065 billion, under President Clinton's proposed fiscal 1998 budget.
The administration proposed raising budget authority for the National Park Service's operating program by six percent, to $1.22 billion from $1.16 billion.

But the budget plan said those funds would not cover increased demands on parks, and the administration said it will seek permanent authority to raise parks fees and will push legislation to reform parks concessions fees.
In the meantime, it will use temporary authority from a pilot program to raise park fees to finance park improvements.
The budget for the Bureau of Land Management would rise to $688 million from $673 million. The Fish and Wildlife Service budget would rise to $562 million from $524 million.

The Minerals Management Service, which oversees leases and royalties and fee collections for oil, natural gas and minerals off federal lands, would get a five percent increase to $743 million in fiscal 1998 from $707 million.
The Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement budget would rise to $327 million from $303 million.
